utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I shall ask Madam Registrar to call the case, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honour, this is case number IT-01-47-T, Enver Hadzihasanovic and Amir Kubura.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. I shall ask the Prosecution to present their case.

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. Good morning, counsel. For the Prosecution, Tecla Benjamin, Ekkehard Withopf, and Ruth Karper the case manager.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. Withopf. I shall now turn to the Defence. Appearances, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Your Honours. On behalf of General Hadzihasanovic, Edina Residovic, counsel, Alexis Demirdjian, assistant, and Stefane Bourgon, co-counsel. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Your Honours. On behalf of Mr. Kubura, Rodney Dixon, Fahrudin Ibrisimovic, and Mr. Mulalic, legal assistant.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. The Chamber would like to welcome all the people present in the courtroom. The Prosecution, the Defence, all the members present in the courtroom, Madam Registrar, the usher, as well as the security guards, as well as the interpreters. Madam Registrar, of course, and thanks to the interpreters, we are able to follow what is going on in this courtroom. We shall now hear the witness, and we will have to move into closed session to begin with.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Witness ZI. I'm called Stefane Bourgon. Mrs. Edina Residovic and Mr. Alexis Demirdjian we are here on behalf of Mr. Hadzihasanovic. You provided your statement as evidence pursuant to Article 92 bis of the Rules of Procedure and Evidence. I shall now proceed with the cross-examination. As the Judge of the Chamber has just explained to you. In other words, I shall ask you a few questions pertaining to the contents of the said statement, as well as the method you use to sketch those drawings which you have filed together with your statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: 1 (Redacted) 2 (Redacted) 3 (Redacted) 4 (Redacted) 5 (Redacted)

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could you please ask the witness where this meeting was held, because you may reveal the identity of the witness by so doing.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I was just going to put a few questions to the witness pertaining to the fact that he had made the statement to the investigators of the Office of the Prosecution, and this could not lead to us understanding what his identity is. So we shall move into private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're in open session, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: According to what you have mentioned to the investigators of the OTP you were in the position to take photos of all the houses that had been destroyed in the period between 1993 and 1994. They were still in the same state of destruction up to the period when the investigation started in 2002; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ZI
utterances.text: No, it's not. We did not take photos. In the statement, it says that the investigator asked me to collect information and to make sketches for myself of all the destroyed buildings; to be more precise, buildings in ten villages, the names of which I can give you. Those are the buildings which were destroyed in 1992 and in 1993. For each of these villages, I was given the exactly precise period of time that was relevant for that village.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise. In the transcript, the year is wrong. The witness mentioned 1992. Then he corrected himself and he said 1993, 1994. In the transcript, in line 9, page 19, it says only 1992, 1993.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Thank you, Witness ZI. I was referring to the -- to another paragraph of your statement, and this is the part referring to the instructions that you received from the investigators of the ICTY. The list of the villages where you were sent to collect information is in the third paragraph of your statement. I would like to confirm with you what were the instructions that you received? In other words, were you supposed to investigate the events which took place in 1993 and 1994 or were you supposed to investigate the destruction that took place in the months that are precisely mentioned in the third paragraph of the statement?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ZI
utterances.text: I was instructed to investigate very specific months, for Dusina, January 1993 to mid-February of the same year; Miletici village, the month was April 1993; Guca Gora, Maljine, Cukle, Donje Cukle, Gornje Cukle, Ovnak, Brajkovici, Grahovcici, June 1993; Buhine Kuce settlement, the relevant period was January 1994.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Thank you, Witness. On the 6th of March, 2002, you knew that two officers of the BiH army had been indicted. Were you aware of the counts of the indictment? Were you aware of the crimes that were allegedly committed in Central Bosnia?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ZI
utterances.text: Yes. I read the indictment and I was aware of most of the things in it.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: So you are also -- you were also aware of the contents of the indictment against General Hadzihasanovic and Alagic at that moment, as well as against Mr. Kubura. The counts that I'm referring to is the destruction of houses in the aforementioned villages. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ZI
utterances.text: I read the indictment. To be honest, I did not ponder on it. My logic told me that the count of destruction should be contained within the indictment.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Thank you, Witness. Before we move to the attachments, I would like to ask you some questions about the methodology that you applied in order to draft the attachment that is attached to your statement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I was just going to say the same. As soon as you mention a name, there is a possibility that somebody might be identified. Therefore, I'm going to ask Madam Registrar to redact the name that has been mentioned, and maybe it will be better if we go into private session, should you again be mentioning names. Mr. Bourgon.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, the Defence would like to remain in open session. We don't think that the fact that we are mentioning the name of a person that may have met with a number of other persons, and if there is no other link between this witness and that person, I don't see the reason for us to be in private session. This person whom we have mentioned testified before this Tribunal without any protective measures, and we don't see how the mere fact that the witness spoke to this person can identify the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Madam Registrar, can we go into private session, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. A while ago, during the cross-examination, the issue of counts 5 and 6 of the indictment pertaining to Dusina were mentioned. These are mentioned in the indictment. The Prosecution stated that in its pre-trial brief, it had dropped this charge. There are several alternatives in this case. The one which complies with the Rules of Procedure and the Statute and the spirit of the legal procedure is as follows: When an indictment is amended, the procedure pursuant to Article 93 needs to be applied. This can be very quick. A paragraph is drafted and then observations are collected and we render a decision. But it is for the Prosecution to take a decision on this. So the Prosecution decides to add, to amend, to modify, to drop. The Trial Chamber, therefore, imparts to the Prosecution that there is a procedure currently applied before this Tribunal, but there is also another alternative, which is to take an oral statement. The Defence submitted that an oral statement is insufficient. The Trial Chamber therefore asks the Prosecution to give this matter some thought. What does the Prosecution intend to do to settle the issue of Dusina? In terms of legal practice and documents we have governing this kind of issue, we have the indictment, on the one hand, and the pre-trial brief, on the other. This is not an urgent matter, but in the meantime, the Prosecution will inform us of its intentions, as the Prosecution here is in control of this matter. I apologise vis-a-vis the interpreters, to have overstepped my time. We would like to thank the interpreters for their cooperation, and I will convene all the parties present to come to the audience tomorrow morning, which will resume tomorrow at 9.00. I think Mr. Bourgon would like to take the floor.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Very briefly, I would like to ask our learned colleague to disclose the photographs to us so that we can prepare our case for tomorrow. This is a minor issue, but we would like to impart our comments vis-a-vis the testimony of some witness by videolink. I don't know if this issue is to be addressed today or whether we should talk about this tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If you are brief, we can address this today. We -- the Trial Chamber has been seized with this matter. If you make your observations orally.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The Defence team of Mr. Kubura will make observations in the name of the two accused people.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Withopf, you have the floor.

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: Also, the Prosecution is very much in favour to discuss this issue now. I would, however, strongly suggest that first the witness leaves the room. This is not an issue the witness is involved in at all.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well, then. Madam Usher, can you please take the witness out of the courtroom. Sir, you are requested to come back tomorrow at 9.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Withopf -- Mr. Dixon, you have the floor.

utterances.speaker: MR. DIXON
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours. I was going to address the issue of the videolink evidence. However, I'm just conscious of the time. I would suggest, Your Honours, that we should rather look at addressing this issue before Your Honours tomorrow at the beginning of the hearing, in order that sufficient time can be given to consider the matter. Because we do have some objections for certain witnesses and we will have to go through those in some detail. It could be done in written form, Your Honour, but I think orally would be quicker and it could be resolved tomorrow morning. There's one other matter as well totally unrelated to this, but perhaps my friend wishes to address Your Honours first.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We are in open session still.

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: In respect to the set of photocopies of the photographs, since my learned colleague asked me to disclose the photographs, I wish to mention for the record that these photographs have been disclosed on the 10th of October, 2003. Defence are in possession of the photographs. The ERN range is 01799933, 01799978, and the PT number in the Rule 65 ter exhibit list is PT1309. However, in order to facilitate the work of my learned colleagues, we are prepared to provide them with two additional sets of hard copies.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Mr. Bourgon. You have the floor. You already have them, I suppose.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. I've mentioned already that I looked at them on the video. We, however, would like to receive a hard copy that we can hold in our hands and look from all sides.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The Prosecution is going to make your life easier and they're going to give the entire bundle of documents. And now, as for the videolink, the Defence would like to address this issue tomorrow. It's 5 minutes to 2.00. I would like to thank everybody. Before that, Mr. Dixon, you have the floor.

utterances.speaker: MR. DIXON
utterances.text: That in fact involves shortening the schedule, which is the schedule tomorrow. Could we go into private session in order to do that?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. We are in open session. We are moving into private session, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In open session, I would like to adjourn for today. I'm inviting all the parties to come back tomorrow at 9.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Friday, the 5th day of March 2004, at 9.00 a.m.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 1.57 p.m.
